correctness.rationale: For F(x,y)=(|x|-y-1,x-|y|-13/16) the exact six-cycle and sixth return to segment Pi=(u,u+3/16), -11/16<=u<=13/16, were independently reconstructed in rational arithmetic. The return is two full branches of slopes 16 and -8 on [-11/16,-19/32] and [-3/16,0], plus two plateaux leading to the periodic endpoint. The inverse contractions 1/16 and 1/8 have strongly separated images and thus their Cantor survivor has Hausdorff and upper box dimension s solving 16^(-s)+8^(-s)=1 (s≈0.287760787084). The graph-entry and graph-visitation assertions are explicitly taken from published Cima–Gasull–Mañosa–Mañosas Theorem B/Proposition27, not re-proved. On piecewise affine graph edges, nonconstant preimage maps are bi-Lipschitz and constant graph branches capture, giving graph exception dimension s. For the full plane, first rank-zero itinerary maps have integer-affine constant values in 16-scaled coordinates and must reach the six-cycle (the only isolated fixed point has unique preimage). Rank-two and rank-one preimages lift the graph Cantor sets by at most 0 and 1 dimensions, with countable affine pieces and boundaries dimension <=1. A positive-quadrant rank-one inverse strip provides a bi-Lipschitz embedded (Cantor exception)x[5,6], proving sharp 1+s. Independent rational checks verified 513 sample sixth returns, all 25 integral interval states, and the orbit; these finite tests support, but do not prove, the graph-entry or dimension theorems.

originality.rationale: The endpoint full-plane exact noncapture dimension is not the previously studied graph recurrence, entropy or full-measure preperiodicity. The primary Cima et al article establishes invariant graph and sixth return and the sequel a measure statement; neither inspected full text states the planar Hausdorff dimension 1+s. The difference between noncapture by *exact finite landing* and asymptotic convergence is essential, and the rank-zero exclusion plus one-dimensional inverse fiber gives an additional implication.
